reason: Focused registration path where title is acquired or confirmed by court order or provincial enactment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registering title acquired by court order or enactment
proposedGroups.reason: The text requires documentation and fee, forwarding to the Registrar General, and an order if title, land identification, and Community Planning Act compliance are satisfactory.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how title acquired or confirmed by court order or enactment may be registered.

reason: Single Registrar General power to bring land under the Act and direct registration without an application.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registrar General order registering land without application

evidenceText: consent in writing of the owner
make an order directing the registrar to register the title

proposedGroups.reason: The text states the conditions for a registration order without application: supporting information, owner consent, and prescribed fee.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State when the Registrar General may direct registration of title without an application.

reason: Cohesive process for determining registration of title to land governed by the Condominium Property Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registering Condominium Property Act land
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover notice, hearing or consent-based hearing dispensation, orders, order delivery, and hearing powers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how the Registrar General may determine and order registration for Condominium Property Act land.

reason: Central land titles rule that registration is needed to pass interests, with a lease exception and title limit.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration required to pass estates or interests
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections state when instruments pass interests, the short-lease exception, registration effect according to tenor, and predecessor-title limits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain why registration is necessary to pass an estate or interest in registered land.

reason: Defines the registered owner status by title register, registered interests, overriding incidents, and fraud exception.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Status of the registered owner shown by the title register

evidenceText: owner who is shown by the title register
free from all other encumbrances, liens, estates or interests

proposedGroups.reason: The text states what title the registered owner holds and which interests remain relevant.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the legal status of a registered owner shown on the title register.

reason: The section separates effects of registration against adverse rights from court relief for prior unregistered access rights.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Registration effect on adverse possession and prescription
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 17(1) bars later adverse possession and limits prescriptive light, easement, right, or profit a prendre claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how registration affects adverse possession and prescriptive rights.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Court relief for prior unregistered access rights
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow court relief for prior unregistered rights of way or access and identify rectification, compensation, costs, and limits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe court relief for prior unregistered rights of way or access.

reason: The section covers mandatory electronic format rules and separate rules on who may submit or use paper exceptions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Designated instruments in electronic format
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require designated electronic submission, bar non-designated electronic submission, and set approved format and technology requirements.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain which instruments must or may be submitted electronically and in what format.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Who may submit electronic instruments and paper exceptions
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify subscriber, mortgage owner, and land surveyor roles and paper-format exceptions with identity or authority evidence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify who may submit electronic instruments and when paper submission is allowed.

reason: Focused rule allowing digitally scanned images of instruments to be filed or registered under specified requirements.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Filing or registering digitally scanned images
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections state eligible scanned-image filing, approved format and technology, and identity or authorization evidence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when an instrument may be filed or registered as a digitally scanned image.

reason: The section separates authentication of electronic-format instruments, scanned images, and reliance or submission rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Authentication of electronic-format instruments
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require subscriber authentication and define the paper instrument possession and material-provision certification.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain what subscriber authentication certifies for an electronic-format instrument.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Authentication of digitally scanned image instruments
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require scanned-image authentication and certify possession of the paper original and an exact complete scan.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain what authentication certifies for a digitally scanned image instrument.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Reliance on execution evidence and separate submitters
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections permit limited reliance on execution certification or affidavits and clarify that authenticator and submitter may differ.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize reliance limits and that authentication and submission may be done by different persons.

reason: Focused subscriber certification rule for execution and marital-status information.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Proof of execution and marital status for electronic instruments
proposedGroups.reason: The text requires specified information and makes its provision a certification of accuracy and possession of prescribed paper documents.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain what proof of execution and marital status information a subscriber certifies.

reason: Single retention duty for paper instruments and accompanying proof documents after electronic authentication.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Retention of documents after electronic authentication

evidenceText: minimum period of time as is required by the regulations

proposedGroups.reason: The section requires retaining the instrument and accompanying proof documents for the regulatory minimum period.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State what documents a subscriber must retain after authenticating an electronic instrument.

reason: Submission of an electronic instrument certifies the submitter is authorized to submit it.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Certification of authority to submit electronic instruments
proposedGroups.reason: The text treats submission by a subscriber or land surveyor as an authority certification.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State what authority certification is made by submitting an electronic instrument.

reason: Electronic instruments received at land titles offices have the same effect as written, signed instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Effect of electronic instruments received at a land titles office

evidenceText: not required to be in writing or to be signed by the parties
has the same effect for all purposes

proposedGroups.reason: The section gives received electronic instruments legal effect despite other Acts or rules of law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the effect of receiving an electronic instrument that is not written or signed.

reason: Focused production duty when the Registrar General requests retained electronic-instrument documents.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Production of retained electronic-instrument evidence
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections authorize inspection requests and require prompt production by subscribers or former subscribers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State when retained electronic-instrument documents must be produced for inspection.

reason: The section separates the subscriber or land surveyor agreement from professional-body prerequisites.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Subscriber or land surveyor agreement with Service New Brunswick
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 17.8(1) requires an agreement covering technology access, duties, liabilities, and electronic funds transfers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify what the Service New Brunswick agreement must cover for electronic submission users.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Professional body agreements for electronic submission access
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require related professional-body agreements before Service New Brunswick enters agreements with lawyers or land surveyors.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the professional-body prerequisites for electronic submission access.

reason: Central instrument-registration workflow with distinct receipt, rejection, title-record, and amendment or Registry Act document stages.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Receipt, acceptance, registration, and rejection of instruments
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover assigned registration details, examination, acceptance, registration, refusal grounds, rejection records, notice, and the section 12(10) limit.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the registrar workflow for receiving, accepting, registering, and rejecting instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Title registration certificates, notices, and parcel identifiers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover cancelling and issuing certificates, Registry Act notices when land enters the Act, and approved parcel identifiers in the title register.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Describe the records created when land or title is registered under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Amending instruments and Registry Act documents affecting registered land
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow amending instruments and Registrar General-ordered registration of Registry Act documents affecting registered land.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how registered instruments may be amended and when Registry Act documents can be registered.
